definition: requests per second returning 2xx with TTLT <= slo_ttlt_ms; 429 and 503 count as offered-and-failed with zero useful completion, never as zero-latency samples
basis: Two thresholds, both fixed from stock FCFS in the saturated round-A run, which predates every arm they will judge. TIGHT is its median: the latency a user actually experiences most of the time. LAX is its p95: the latency already tolerated in the tail. Both are reported because the choice decides the answer -- a lax cutoff makes shedding look harmful since nearly everything passes anyway, a tight one makes it look helpful. Reporting one would be selecting the verdict; reporting both shows how sensitive the verdict is to a number nobody can derive from first principles.
frozen_before: the overload arm (C') and any 15 ms contract arm (B)
reporting_rule: goodput at both thresholds, side by side, with the rejection rate and the status breakdown that produced it
